title: Where bands played, societies, pay and prices
summary: Bands played in halls and parades for societies; pay was around twelve dollars for the band or less, and he recalls how far a dime or nickel went.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: When you were youngsters, where would the brass bands be playing? Huh? When you were a youngster, where would the brass bands be playing? Would they play out in the streets?

Oh no, they played in the hall. In the hall? That's how we used to play. We used to play all in the Orleans, I don't know, it took so long. We used to play parade. Play all over. Way back, way back to the country. We used to go down there and lick. And there's two-two boys way up the road there. That's right.
Did they play parades in this neighborhood or around the...

Around the other, sure the society would turn out, you know. What societies would they have? Oh, they had Japanese arms, they had friends of the whole world. He's alive, they got so many of them. Vetson, they got twenty or more.
Yeah, they hired them. Well, they used to play for nothing. I would get twelve dollars down.
Twelve dollars for the whole band? The whole band, dollar.

No, that ain't no way to play for no, I used to play in the city there. I didn't make a band for six, seventy-five cents. Seventy-five cents, so I wouldn't get nothing.
Well that was money in those days.
Yeah, money, yeah. It wasn't much. I come first, I don't know. Have a pint, have a pint in with a dime. Yeah.
You could stay drunk on that.

Yeah, that was a dime. Make that fifty cents, buy a $1 grocery. Yeah, that's right, $1 grocery. You had kvati rice, kvati meat and all that. Yeah, kvati flour, sugar, everything, you know. Yeah, that was a dime though. Yeah. A meal around myself for 80 cents, so you could get it there for 15 cents. That's right. Now you go in a restaurant and get a meal around for about 81 cents or something like that. Yeah. 15 cents, you got all you wanted to eat, couldn't eat it. That's right.
